rateHero.name: Ilkin Ibadov
rateHero.lede: Rates and terms by type of work. The figures below are grounded in the scope and nature of work I deliver in practice — the “Track record” section gives verifiable numbers.

trackRecord.title: Track record
trackRecord.intro: Aggregate figures across three product projects. The numbers come from repository history and source code, not from a CV description.

skills.title: Skills & stack
skills.intro: The technologies the projects below are built on. Web, mobile and infrastructure in one pair of hands.

setflow.summary: Multi-tenant CRM + warehouse platform: deals and pipelines, double-entry stock movements, documents and quotes, omnichannel inbox, campaigns, subscriptions. Live in production on its own domain.

brain.summary: Meditation and self-development platform: mobile app, API, content admin panel and storefront in a single monorepo. Audio and media served from S3 object storage.

qala.summary: Services marketplace: matching workers to orders, two role-based interfaces (client and worker), chat with attachments, reviews. Two-factor auth, documented API, business plan prepared for Astana Hub.

note.strong: The work is end-to-end, not single-specialisation.
note.text: Two of the three products were built solo — from database schema and API through to the mobile app and deployment; in SetFlow the commits split almost evenly between frontend and backend. That is the main reason the rate sits above a single-layer developer’s: the client doesn’t need a second person, or the coordination between them.

fullTime.title: Full-time employment
fullTime.text: Full-time, full ownership of a domain. Below the hourly equivalent — that discount buys stability and long-term product ownership.

partTime.title: Part-time
partTime.text: 20–25 hrs/week on fixed days. Fits when you need a strong engineer but not a full-time one.

retainer.title: Support retainer
retainer.text: Agreed hour bank, priority response, security updates. Unused hours roll over one month.

fixedPrice.title: Fixed-price project
fixedPrice.text: Fixed price where scope is well defined. The premium covers uncertainty risk; hourly work carries none.

legacy.why: Time goes to comprehension before change

included.title: What the rate includes
included: Meaningful commit messages and review turnaround
Fixing my own bugs — free for 30 days
Handover: how it works and why it’s built that way
billed: Meetings beyond one hour per week
Maintaining code I did not write

items.text: A task goes from database to interface without a handoff — saving not just the second salary but the coordination time around it.

items.strong: Web and mobile aren’t separate hires.
items.text: Two React Native apps (67 screens) and React web interfaces over a shared backend: one codebase of types and contracts instead of two teams reconciling an API between them.
A modular monolith, a multi-app monorepo and a set of NestJS microservices — the approach is chosen to fit the problem, not out of habit with one stack.
Domains and DNS, CDN, mail infrastructure, incident response on live traffic — the work doesn’t end at merge.

items.strong: Security as part of the job.
items.text: Tenant data isolation, webhook signature verification, closing dependency vulnerabilities — with findings verified against a live system, not copied from a scanner report.
The claims above are backed by repository history and test suites, not by a CV description.

note.text: The lower bound is a well-defined task in a familiar stack. The upper bound is tight deadlines, unfamiliar code, or a high cost of failure. Rates are negotiable: scope, duration and predictability move them more than the category of work does.
